evidenceAudit.scope: Women in labour: choosing intermittent auscultation or CTG, classifying the CTG, conservative measures and expediting birth for suspected fetal compromise. Verified against NICE NG229 (fetal monitoring in labour, 2022, updated 2025); the Saudi MOH Pocket Manual has no dedicated intrapartum CTG chapter.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Fetal blood sampling — NICE makes no recommendation
Saudi MOH intrapartum CTG guidance not found

pathophysiology.summary: Intrapartum fetal compromise is hypoxia developing during labour, when contractions intermittently reduce placental blood flow. A healthy fetus tolerates this; a fetus with reduced reserve, or one exposed to excessive contractions, cord compression or acute events, can become acidotic.
keyMechanisms: Each contraction transiently reduces uteroplacental flow; too-frequent contractions (5 or more in 10 minutes or hypertonus) shorten recovery time (NICE).
Cord compression causes variable decelerations; uteroplacental insufficiency causes late decelerations.
Developing hypoxia or infection raises the baseline heart rate; worsening hypoxia reduces variability (NICE).
Acute events — cord prolapse, abruption, uterine rupture — cause sudden bradycardia.

symptoms: Often none; meconium-stained liquor, fever, bleeding, abdominal pain or slow progress raise concern (NICE lists slow progress, sepsis, meconium).
physicalSigns: Fetal heart abnormalities on auscultation or CTG.
Maternal tachycardia, fever, hypotension; abnormal uterine tone.
redFlags: Acute bradycardia or a single prolonged deceleration of 3 minutes or more
Cord prolapse, suspected abruption or uterine rupture
No acceleration after fetal scalp stimulation

differentials.condition: Maternal heart rate recorded as fetal
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Accelerations in second stage often maternal — confirm fetal heart at least every 5 minutes (NICE).
Short periods of reduced variability are normal.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: After a contraction for at least 1 minute: every 15 min in first stage, every 5 min in second stage
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Rise of 20 beats/min or more from start of labour, or a deceleration heard.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Auscultate more often; if concern persists advise continuous CTG (NICE).

clinicalManagement.title: Choose monitoring
actions: Assess antenatal risk factors; low risk → intermittent auscultation; risk factors → continuous CTG (NICE NG229).
Return to auscultation if CTG started for auscultation concerns is normal after 20 minutes (unless the woman prefers CTG).

clinicalManagement.title: Hourly review
actions: Assess fetal wellbeing every hour with the whole clinical picture; categorise the CTG.
Normal: continue usual care. Suspicious without other risk factors: full assessment and conservative measures.
Suspicious with slow progress, sepsis or meconium: urgent obstetric review; consider scalp stimulation or expediting birth.

clinicalManagement.title: Conservative measures
actions: Mobilise or change position; avoid supine.
IV fluids only if hypotensive or septic; epidural hypotension → fluids, left lateral, anaesthetist.
5 or more contractions in 10 minutes: reduce or stop oxytocin; offer tocolysis — terbutaline 0.25 mg SC.
Do not give maternal facial oxygen for fetal concerns; do not use amnioinfusion (NICE).

clinicalManagement.title: Pathological CTG or acute bradycardia
actions: Urgent obstetric and senior midwife review; exclude cord prolapse, abruption, uterine rupture.
Still pathological after conservative measures → consider expediting birth.
Acute bradycardia/prolonged deceleration: prepare for urgent birth with neonatal support; expedite if it persists for 9 minutes (sooner with risk factors); document decision times.
Second stage: obstetric review; consider stopping pushing and oxytocin unless birth is imminent.

learningObjectives: Monitor fetal wellbeing in labour, classify CTGs and act on suspected compromise.

keyPoints: Treat the cause: position, fluids if hypotensive, stop oxytocin, terbutaline 0.25 mg SC.
No facial oxygen for fetal concerns.
pitfalls: Recording maternal pulse as fetal heart.
Oxygen to the mother for CTG changes.
Delaying review of a pathological CTG.

patientEducation: Explain monitoring choice and its trade-offs.
Discuss findings and decisions with the woman and companion.
mdtReferrals: Senior obstetrician and midwife for pathological CTG.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Neonatal review after birth following suspected compromise; keep CTG traces 25 years (NICE).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: One red feature or two or more amber
Acute bradycardia persisting 9 minutes (sooner with risk factors)
